product_from_film: Armature monitors and tests how AI agents use a product, then gives alerts, comparisons and improvement recommendations.
explains_well: A wrong-tool example, hidden-failure contrast and later recommendation cards make agent usability problems concrete.
unclear: The film shows several diagnostic outputs but does not carry one failure through a change and a successful retest.

categories.finding: Failed MCP launch → hidden tool ambiguity → Armature → monitor/alert → workflow/tests/benchmark → recommendations → agent-user thesis → CTA.
A connected green system and Push MCP action create a concrete launch setup before red errors appear.
The monitoring dashboard at 34s makes the product function clear; MCP and tool examples address teams building agent-facing products.
Connection states, red/green statuses, workflow steps, test-grid cells and recommendation cards change visibly; exact easing and execution timing are unverified.
The dark failure section switches to a light solution section at 27s; repeated tool names/cards preserve technical continuity.
Flat dark/cream surfaces, thin outlines, orange accents and restrained red/green statuses create a diagram-led style.
Specific wrong-tool and recommendation text makes the argument concrete. Dashboard details and comparison numbers are smaller than the supporting headlines.

categories.finding: Text and status diagrams make the problem and output types readable silently. The fix/retest loop is not shown.
The wrong-tool example and alerts are isolated in close cards; the model grid and benchmark table broaden the view before recommendations narrow it again.
About 27s establish failure and trust loss, then about 25s demonstrate monitoring through recommendations before the final thesis/CTA.
Opaque failures are answered by named workflows, test results and recommendations, but the opening ambiguity is not visibly repaired.
Hidden failure versus an all-good signal may evoke developer frustration; audience reaction is unmeasured.
Cards, tool names and status colors make the technical story coherent; the examples change rather than tracking one issue throughout.
Monitoring coverage, benchmark scores, recommendation efficacy and setup time are film claims. No live-system performance or competitor comparison was independently checked.
The agent-as-user framing and specific tool-ambiguity example distinguish the story from generic observability messaging.
Close the loop by applying one recommendation and rerunning the original failed task.
